rationale: ADJUDICATED 2026-08-24 by viewing the image. The meme is a FLATTERING portrait of Gebran Bassil - his name and party across the top, and 'على سرمايتك ما حدا بغبّر' (nobody can raise dust on your shoe) along the bottom. So 'ma fi 8ayron' means BASSIL is the best, posted at someone who had just criticised him: dismissive of the author. An earlier reading that the meme mocked Bassil was wrong. expectedBaselineLabel is Negative because the sarcastic text alone already reads Negative - this is a harm case, not a lift case.

rationale: ADJUDICATED 2026-08-24 by viewing the image. The smiling man giving a thumbs-up IS Gebran Bassil. The caption 'ما بيحكي بالسوء عنك الا يلي رح يموت قهر منك' (only the one who will die of spite speaks ill of you) is therefore aimed at Bassil's critic - the author of the post. An earlier reading calling it a supportive meme was wrong; the face was not recognised. LIFT case: text alone is Neutral, media should make it Negative. The live pass frequently returns Positive here, which is the sharpest known failure.

phenomenon: FLAGSHIP LIFT - image-only insult, invisible to text-only analysis
rationale: The reply is a bare mention plus two images. The first advertises the phone number of دير الصليب, the Lebanese psychiatric hospital - a standard way of calling someone insane. The second is a crude cartoon reading 'رأيك وطيزنا سوا' (your opinion and our backside are the same). Text-only MUST return Neutral and media MUST return Negative. This is the clearest case for the whole feature: if it fails, the feature has no value.

rationale: A bare mention plus a video. Only the thumbnail is available - a man in a room, no text - so there is no evidence either way. The correct behaviour is Neutral. This case exists to prove the pipeline does NOT invent a label from a thumbnail it cannot read; any Negative here is a false positive.
